scores.design: uniform.md (semantic uniformity first: tree-shaped KIR, shared LIR lowering, state-word propagation + yield bubbling on all backends, logical depth)
scores.strengths: Fits the owner's goals best on the parts that are architecture rather than scheduling. (1) The IR is small for Diktor to emit. KIR is a tree at Diktor's own level with reps only (3.1, 3.2, D501/D502), and ANF, box/unbox, decision trees, numeric checks and effect lowering are done once in the shared Rust LIR (6.4). The Diktor emitter stays a near 1:1 walk (tree §1.4), and the later Rust frontend only has to reproduce this light KIR. Diktor estimate is 3.1-4.9k code lines including a reference evaluator (5.1), comparable to the others. (2) The interpreter/LLVM mutual jump uses tier-independent frame records: a frame captured by either tier can resume in either tier through entry[id] (6.9). It also reuses the measured ABI `tailcc i64 (ptr ctx)` (D518, tg §3.3 E6: 1e8 alternating tail calls under `ulimit -s 512`). (3) One effect mechanism on all three backends (D508, D509, 6.6). `rt_handle`/`rt_resume` are written once as LIR builtins, so the cancel-ordering cases (cancelperform, cancelsame, cancelresume, retry) are implemented once and traced in 6.6.6. (4) Logical depth (D512, 3.13) is the only proposal that lets ki, kj, ka and kw be byte-identical, and 8.2 makes that a hard rule independent of known diffs. (5) Risk comes first: M79 is a spike with runnable pass/fail commands for the Node RLIMIT_STACK/--stack-size depth and for the wasm32 target (9 M79). (6) The frontend (M90) depends only on M82, so it can run in parallel with the backends. The KIR-text equality check against Diktor is cheap because names are stable symbols with relative-path unit keys (3.3). (7) The details are careful: D535 init-check elision with a named counterexample, D511/V191 for resume(resume(x)), and the may_yield prune with a `--no-yield-prune` cross-check (D526).
scores.flaws: (a) The WasmGC runtime plan is blocked by the current toolchain. D515, 6.10 and P239 compile `keleut-rt-core` to wasm32-unknown-unknown, but this machine has only `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` under `$(rustc --print sysroot)/lib/rustlib` and no rustup (I checked; native.md's header records the same). The fallback of committing a prebuilt rt.wasm with hash and provenance is weak for a repository that is built from source. (b) Milestones are too large to verify one at a time: M83 is 8-11k lines (rt-core, rt, LIR passes 1-7/9/10/12, interpreter, kconform v0), M86 LLVM is 6-8k, M88 WasmGC is 7-9k. There is no vertical slice such as 'no user handle' (compare incremental M80/M81). (c) The WasmGC depth target of 1M non-tail frames rests on V198 (RLIMIT_STACK plus a large --stack-size). sw §2 measured SIGSEGV at --stack-size=65500. M79 checks this, but if it fails, the cross-backend identity rule in 8.2 breaks and P245 falls back to a shallower limit plus a known diff. (d) Yield bubbling copies every frame between the perform and the handler on each G perform and re-enters each one on resume. That is O(depth) per G perform, and every non-pruned call site in JIT and Wasm needs a resume switch, which grows code size (6.4 step 12, 6.10). This cost is only measured at M89. (e) The `libm` crate on all RustKeleut backends deliberately differs from the Diktor oracle (glibc) for sin/cos/exp/log (D527, V193). It is honestly registered, but it removes oracle coverage that incremental keeps natively. (f) M80 changes Diktor's tree evaluator (the nested-resume fix) inside the emitter milestone. It should be its own small commit or milestone. (g) No acceptance criterion measures compile speed (`keleut check` against `diktor --type-check`), even though compile speed is the owner's stated motive.
scores.score_note: Strongest semantics and backend fit, but blocked WasmGC runtime route and oversized milestones.

scores.design: native.md (native performance first: Kerno ANF IR, fibers for native G, register-arg ABI, JSPI for Wasm G)
scores.strengths: (1) The measurement table E1-E20 (section 1) indexes the evidence well, and every decision cites an E-number. (2) It is the only proposal that analyses typed returns against tail calls (2.3). It chooses always-`w` returns so a call from an i64-returning f to a w-returning polymorphic g stays a tail call, and records the unboxed-return optimization as V193. Any final design should adopt this analysis. (3) It measured the wasm32 gap itself and found a working route: clang 22 --target=wasm32 plus wasm-ld, producing a 295-byte module (header and section 13), used for musl libm.wasm (4.10, P246). (4) For the unmeasured ABI it states an explicit gate: re-measure the alternating tail calls with the 6-argument prototype first in M87, else revert to the measured `tailcc i64 (ptr ctx)` (D535). (5) Fibers make native continuations tier-agnostic without a shared frame format, and Rust-written builtins can be suspended (4.8, 4.9). (6) The sentinel 0x2 return for unwinding (D531) is cheap and well argued against DWARF unwinding (cost per throw on retry.kel). (7) Diktor effort is reasonable at 2.9-4.6k lines (3.1), and the `DIKTOR_EXEC=ir dune runtest` gate (3.3) is a good self-check.
scores.flaws: (a) The IR freeze is unexecutable. M79 freezes IRSpec 1.0 (the 7.2 table: 'doc/IRSpec.md（版 1.0 の凍結…)', and 2.8 'versions 1.0 frozen at M79') before any emitter or reader exists, and its acceptance is '所有者が読む', which nobody can verify. 2.8 also says major 0 may change freely until then, which contradicts freezing first. (b) The primary WasmGC G mechanism contradicts its own sources. D541 and 4.10 choose JSPI, but effects-impl.md:317 says a suspended Wasm stack cannot be resumed synchronously from the Wasm side, and tiering-gc.md:432 calls JSPI too heavy for deep handlers. The fallback to bubbling is only decided at M90, after M89 has been built around exnref plus JSPI. (c) Three effect implementations: fibers natively (D538/D539), exnref plus JSPI on Wasm, and possibly bubbling. The cancel-ordering logic (fx R5, Q5) has to be written and verified two or three times, which works against byte equality across backends. (d) The load-bearing ABI is unmeasured: D535 passes 6 register arguments, while E6 measured only the 1-argument form. (e) The WasmGC depth default is half a startup-probed RangeError depth, falling back to 4,000 (D543), against Diktor's ~1M. W will diverge from D and K* on a broad class of deep-recursion inputs, and there is no plan to make it uniform. JIT does not count depth by default (D530), so even KI and KJ limits can differ. (f) Native uses the Rust `libm` crate and Wasm uses musl C. V203 compares those two, but the difference from the Diktor oracle (glibc) is never registered as a known diff (I grepped native.md: glibc appears only for show_f64). (g) Diktor must emit ANF plus box/unbox (2.2, 2.3), and the Rust frontend must reproduce that byte-identically. It is more Diktor work and one more place for the two emitters to disagree. (h) Milestone jumps are large: M84 has no effects, then M85 brings all of N/T/G, fibers, cancel and the depth limit at once. M83 builds the fiber pool and GC before any interpreter can exercise them. M94 adds a REPL, which is scope beyond the request. (i) No compile-speed benchmark.
scores.score_note: Several load-bearing choices go against evidence or are unverified.

scores.design: incremental.md (end-to-end first, risk paid early: KIR ANF with structured control, value-stack segments, JIT falls back to interpreter on YIELD/UNWIND)
scores.strengths: (1) The best milestone slicing for verifiability. The Diktor lowering first excludes user `handle` (M80/M81), with full effects added in M84 in parallel with M83. JIT first excludes functions containing handle/resume (D547, M87) and adds them in M89. WasmGC does N/T first (M90, with G programs exiting 4 as a registered diff) and G second (M91). The frontend is split into 5 gated milestones (M93-M97), each tied to named cram files. (2) End-to-end first: M83 already runs real cram through the shim. M82 may start from `kir_bin` before `kir_eval` (6.2 M82). `--frontend=diktor` (3.2) makes the CLI and the shim their final shape from day one. (3) D542 is a clever tiering idea. The JIT frame layout equals the interpreter frame layout, so on YIELD or UNWIND the JIT frames simply return and the interpreter continues them. G capture becomes deoptimization for free, with no fibers and no landing pads. (4) It uses glibc libm natively (D539), so native output matches the Diktor oracle, and the Wasm difference is isolated (P233). (5) D514 writes Array.each, pinned and with_runtime as KIR runtime functions, so continuations cross builtins naturally. (6) It shares the decision tree before the backends diverge (D529, M86). It has a known-diffs file that fails on any unregistered mismatch (D562), a broken-KIR corpus (5.4), and IR-table cross-checks (D514). (7) Diktor effort is 2.8-4.2k code lines, and the literate-style cost is stated explicitly (2.1).
scores.flaws: (a) Typed returns break tail calls. D510 and D545 return raw i32/i64/f64/bool bits when the declared return rep is unboxed, and `ref` only from the uniform entry. A tail call from an i64-returning function to a ref-returning polymorphic function, or the reverse, then needs a box/unbox after the call, so it cannot be `musttail`. That violates LangSpec §5.7 (native 2.3 shows the exact case). The proposal never addresses this. (b) The frontend is gated behind the hardest backend work. M93 depends on M92 (KIR 1.0 freeze), and M92 depends on M85, M89 and M91 (WasmGC G state machines) (6.3 graph). The compile-speed benefit, which is the owner's actual motive, arrives last, and a stall in M91 blocks it. (c) The WasmGC effect mechanism differs from native: exnref try_table plus state-machine bubbling (D555, D556) against value-stack segments plus unwind frames (D540, D541). Cancel ordering (Q2-Q5) is implemented twice. (d) Stack limits are unverified and brittle. D537 counts value-stack words to match OCaml's `l=` and admits it does not know Diktor's default limit (fid §5 measured 100M frames). D561 maps OCAMLRUNPARAM through the shim with frame-header tuning in M85. Wasm depth is left as a possible known diff (V199). It also reserves a 4 GiB native stack thread, with a WSL2 overcommit risk in its own risk table. (e) Index-by-traversal-order naming (D505), with Diktor's process-specific unit numbering (D504), forces the Rust frontend to reproduce Diktor's exact traversal order for byte-equal KIR. Symbolic names (uniform 3.3) are more robust. (f) Diktor must emit ANF plus box/unbox (2.2 steps 6-7), which raises Diktor work and the cost of matching the Rust emitter. (g) There is no early spike for the known unknowns (Node stack size, Worker stackSizeMb, 4 GiB reservation, JS BigInt show speed) despite the 'risk prepayment' framing. M83 is large (rt, GC, vm, shim and conform together). (h) Float64 show is implemented twice (Rust D534 and JS BigInt D553), which doubles the 2M-case verification. (i) No compile-speed benchmark.
scores.score_note: Best plan to execute, but has the tail-call return-rep hole and gates the frontend behind WasmGC.

best_ideas: uniform D512/3.13 + 8.2: define a logical depth limit (count of non-tail calls, default 1,000,000), count it identically in Diktor --run-ir and all RustKeleut backends, and require ki=kj=ka=kw byte-identical output regardless of known diffs against Diktor's tree evaluator.

uniform 6.6: one effect/escape protocol (state word + rt_handle/rt_resume as LIR builtins) shared by interpreter, JIT and WasmGC so the cancel-ordering cases (never_ops cancelresume family, resumeinner*, retry) are implemented once; uniform 6.6.6 table mapping each hard cram case to the protocol.

incremental D542: make JIT frame layout identical to interpreter frames on the shared value stack so that YIELD/UNWIND just returns out of JIT frames and the interpreter continues them; continuation capture becomes free deoptimization and continuations are tier-agnostic without fibers or landing pads.

uniform 3.1/3.2 + 6.4: keep KIR tree-shaped with Rep annotations only; do ANF, box/unbox, decision trees, numeric checks and effect lowering once in the shared Rust LIR, minimizing Diktor emitter work and the surface the Rust frontend must reproduce byte-identically.
uniform 3.3: stable symbolic names (unit key = relative path / qualified name#n) instead of traversal-order indices, so Diktor and Rust emitters can be compared by canonical KIR text robustly.
native 2.3: analysis that unboxed return reps break tail-call guarantees; v1 returns are always uniform words, unboxed-return entries deferred as an optimization.
native header/section 13: route C sources (musl libm, possibly float show) through clang --target=wasm32 + wasm-ld, which was measured to work, instead of relying on an absent Rust wasm32 target.

native D535: explicit gate 're-measure the alternating musttail test first with the new ABI, else revert to the measured tailcc i64 (ptr ctx)'; native section 1 E-table of measurements cited by every decision.

incremental slicing: Diktor lowering without user handle first (M80/M81), JIT excluding handler-containing functions first (D547), WasmGC without G clauses first with G programs exiting 4 as registered known diffs (M90), frontend split by cram gates (M93-M97).

incremental 3.2/D560: --frontend=diktor delegation and a PATH shim so the CLI and cram harness have their final shape from the first runnable milestone; M82 can start once kir_bin lands without waiting for kir_eval.
incremental D514/D538 and uniform D533: write Array.each, pinned and runtime wiring as KIR library code so continuations and tier switches work inside builtins.

incremental D539: native extern C math via system glibc so native results match the Diktor oracle; uniform D535 init-check elision rule with its named counterexample as a conformance test; uniform M79 as a risk-first spike milestone with runnable pass/fail commands.
incremental D562: known-diffs registry that fails on any unregistered mismatch, plus broken-KIR corpus and IR-table cross-check (D514, 5.4).
must_fix: Wasm runtime toolchain: this machine has no wasm32 Rust target (rustlib contains only x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, no rustup). The final design must pick a route that builds from source here: clang+wasm-ld C (measured to work), JS, or an explicit install step with a check in the first milestone. Committing a prebuilt rt.wasm is not acceptable as the default.

Tail calls vs return representation: either all function returns are the uniform word in v1 (native 2.3, uniform 6.4 step 4), or the plan must show how a tail call between functions with different return reps stays musttail. Incremental D510/D545 as written violates §5.7.

Owner's motive is compile speed: add an acceptance gate that measures keleut check / keleut emit-kir against diktor --type-check on a large input (e.g. sample.kel plus the 1,046-file corpus). Make the frontend milestones depend only on the KIR reader/printer (M82 equivalent), not on LLVM or WasmGC completion.
Freeze KIR 1.0 only after both Diktor and RustKeleut read and write it and the corpus round-trips. Never freeze it in the first, documentation-only milestone (native M79).

Use one effect/continuation mechanism for interpreter and JIT that is tier-agnostic: shared frame records or the shared frame layout of incremental D542. Do not mix fibers on native with a different scheme on Wasm unless cancel ordering (fx Q2-Q5, never_ops cancelresume family) is verified per backend. Prefer the same propagation protocol on WasmGC too.

Do not make JSPI or WasmFX the primary WasmGC G mechanism. effects-impl.md:317 and tiering-gc.md:432 rule out JSPI for synchronous resume, and WasmFX is flagged and crashes. Use bubbling/state machines over GC structs.

Stack/depth limit policy must be decided before conformance expectations are set. Spike Node RLIMIT_STACK + --stack-size (and Worker stackSizeMb) in the first milestone. Define a logical depth counted identically by every backend and by diktor --run-ir. Exclude the OCaml-stack-limited cram blocks explicitly rather than mapping OCAMLRUNPARAM words.
Use the call ABI that was measured (tailcc i64 (ptr ctx), E6) unless the first JIT milestone re-measures an alternative under ulimit -s 512 with a revert rule.

State the libm policy relative to the Diktor oracle. Either use glibc natively and register the Wasm difference, or use one shared implementation everywhere and register the difference against Diktor. Native leaves the D vs K* difference unregistered.

Cap milestone size (about 3-4k lines) and slice by feature: no user handle, then T/N, then G; JIT without handler functions first; WasmGC without G first. Each milestone needs a runnable acceptance command. Split uniform M83/M86/M88, native M85/M87, incremental M83.

Keep Diktor work bounded and separately committed: emitter, binary, reference evaluator, a via-IR mode over the existing cram, with smoke.t usage updates and expectation updates in their own commits. Land the resume(resume(x)) tree-evaluator fix (V191) as its own small commit with a cram block. Prefer a KIR level that does not force Diktor to emit ANF and box/unbox.

Use stable symbolic names in KIR (unit key + qualified name + ordinal), not Diktor's process-specific unit numbers or traversal-order indices, so that Rust and Diktor emitters can be compared byte-for-byte.

Trap-free lowering must be explicit and checked: zero division, MIN/-1, f64->int range and NaN, array bounds, ref.cast and null must be checked before the instruction in the LIR or the Wasm emitter. A Wasm checker test should assert that no trapping instruction is left unguarded, because traps and stack overflow cannot be caught inside Wasm (fx section 4).

One shared verification-failure exit code and the full exit-code table (0/1/2/3/4/64/74, plus 65 or 70) must be fixed in IRSpec. Use one Float64 show algorithm verified on the 2,000,000-case corpus for every backend, and Diktor's runtime error texts so the cram files pass unmodified.

scores.strengths: Uses only mechanisms the spikes measured, or that follow directly from them. One prototype, tailcc i64(ptr ctx), on every JIT function, which is the form tg 3.3 measured for 1e8 alternating interp/JIT tail calls under ulimit -s 512 (6.8, D518). No statepoints, which avoids the measured breakage of musttail under rewrite-statepoints-for-gc (6.5, D517). No JSPI, WasmFX or exnref, so nothing depends on flagged or crashing V8 features (D508, D520). Escapes and G capture both go through one state word in all three backends (6.6.2-6.6.5). Frame records do not depend on the tier, so a continuation captured in one tier resumes in the other (6.9). The Wasm re-entry mechanism is the only concrete one of the three: an acyclic LIR becomes a flat stack of nested blocks, entered by a br_table at the function head (6.10). That layout really can reach any block start, because br targets enclosing labels and topological nesting puts every later block's label around earlier code. The logical depth limit, the same in every backend (3.13, D512), is the only proposal whose stack-limit outcome is deterministic across tiers and backends. Its Node plan (raise RLIMIT_STACK, then --stack-size, D521/V198) is correct: I measured ulimit -s 2000000 with node --stack-size=1500000 running the spike's even_nt to the search cap of 1e7 frames, and a Worker with resourceLimits.stackSizeMb=1024 also reached 1e7. Frame layout is shared by interp and JIT (6.7). Risks are listed honestly, including the missing wasm32 target (section 10).
scores.flaws: (1) D515/6.10: rt.wasm is built from keleut-rt-core for wasm32-unknown-unknown, but the measured toolchain has no such target ($(rustc --print sysroot)/lib/rustlib has only x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, there is no rustup, and pacman -Q rust-wasm says the package is not installed). Its fallback, committing a binary rt.wasm, is weak. clang 22 --target=wasm32 with wasm-ld is the measured route (native.md header). (2) 6.9: the interp-to-JIT tail transition says only that interp_run returns a 'tail-call request' to the stub. That is valid only when the calling frame is the bottom frame of that interp_run activation. Otherwise outer interpreted frames are still live in the same Rust activation, and the frame must be popped and the JIT called natively (native 4.8 states this rule; uniform does not). (3) 6.5 and 6.10: the 1 KiB-per-logical-level budget for the native and V8 stacks is assumed, not measured. When interp and JIT alternate non-tail, every level nests a Rust interp_run frame plus a stub plus a JIT frame. Liftoff frames for large LIR functions, where every LIR register becomes a wasm local, can exceed 1 KiB. Either way the native stack or V8 overflows before the logical limit. On Wasm that is an uncatchable RangeError (fx 4), so exit 70 instead of 3 and no cancel. kconform would only warn. (4) The single prototype says how the generic interp_stub learns the callee id only through 'the entry table'. It needs a ctx->callee field written before every indirect musttail. (5) The cost stacks up and is never measured together: all arguments go through the in-memory value stack, every function entry checks resume_frame, every non-tail call checks pending and runs depth_inc/dec, and in v1 every function boundary is any, so every Int64 or Float64 argument and return is boxed (6.4 step 4). The JIT may gain little over the interpreter. Benchmarks come only at M89. (6) Yield bubbling copies the whole frame window on each G perform, which is O(depth) per perform. That is accepted but not quantified.

scores.strengths: The native half is sound and measured: corosensei fibers, 1.8 ns per round trip, pooled because a fresh mmap costs 7.1 µs (E9). Fibers suspend interp frames, JIT frames and Rust builtin frames alike (4.9), so neither tier needs resume entry points. A 0x2 sentinel in the return register gives a one-instruction check with no ctx reload (D531). Function returns are always the uniform word, with the explicit argument that a raw return breaks proper tail calls through closures and polymorphic callees (2.3). This is a real hazard the other designs underweight. The interp-to-JIT tail-call rule distinguishes the bottom frame of an activation from a non-bottom frame (4.8), which is correct and complete. Section 1 (E1-E20) maps each decision to the measurement behind it. The register-argument prototype has a measured fallback condition (D535). The rule 'a cancel clause runs once when the unwind's destination is not this activation' (4.9) collapses clauseerr, clausestop and so.kel into one check. It notes the missing Rust wasm32 std, and that clang can emit wasm32.
scores.flaws: (1) D543 rejects raising the main-thread stack on the strength of E15 (--stack-size=65500 gave SIGSEGV). That segfault came from the default 8 MiB RLIMIT_STACK. I measured ulimit -s 2000000 with --stack-size=1500000 reaching 1e7 non-tail wasm frames, and a Worker with stackSizeMb=1024 also reaching 1e7. The startup probe that halves the RangeError depth, with a default of 4000 levels, is therefore unnecessary. It is also nondeterministic across machines and Node versions, and 250x shallower than the 1e6 Diktor sustains, so deep-recursion conformance diverges. (2) D541: G on JSPI is unproven, and the mechanism has a hole. Each JSPI stack is fixed at 984 KB because --experimental-wasm-growable-stacks is off by default (fx 4), but the global depth counter is calibrated on the main stack. Recursion inside a G handler body overflows its JSPI stack before the counter fires, and that overflow cannot be caught. Every resume needs at least two promise/microtask hops plus a JS-side scheduler for nested and forwarding G handlers. None of this has been prototyped with cancel ordering (cancelresume*). (3) If JSPI fails, the fallback is yield bubbling for Wasm only. The effect semantics, including the subtle Q5 cases, would then be built twice: fibers natively, bubbling or JSPI on Wasm. The two backends would also have different continuation shapes. (4) Tier-dependent stack limits: by default the JIT checks only native sp, while the interpreter checks value-stack words (D530, 4.6). Whether a deep program ends with exit 0 or exit 3 then depends on when functions tier up. --depth-limit exists but is off by default. (5) Two maths implementations hoped to match bit for bit: the Rust libm crate natively and musl C compiled by clang on Wasm (D528, V203). The libm crate is a port that has drifted in places. show_f64 is also written twice, in Rust and in JS BigInt. (6) M79 freezes IRSpec 1.0 before any producer or consumer exists, which is implausible. (7) Fibers: 64 MiB NORESERVE plus a guard page plus a paired value stack each, with an active cap of 100,000. That is fine here (vm.max_map_count measured at 1,048,576), but on a stock 65,530 limit the cap fails at roughly 16k-32k fibers. At least 8 KiB of committed pages per fiber is about 800 MB at the cap. (8) The 6-argument register convention is unmeasured for alternating tail calls (acknowledged, with a fallback).

scores.strengths: The best risk staging. Milestones are end to end: Diktor writes KIR, the RustKeleut interpreter runs it, and the cram shim checks the result (M79-M86) before the JIT or Wasm are built. Diktor gets a reference IR evaluator. The first JIT compiles only functions without handle or resume, and T clauses stay in the interpreter (D547). That keeps tailcc/musttail risk apart from effect risk. 'Deopt on yield' (D542) is a clever graft. JIT frames have the same layout as interpreter frames on the value stack, so a YIELD or UNWIND just returns to interp_run and the interpreter continues those frames. The JIT needs no resume entries, no fibers, no eh_frame and no landing pads. --tier=mixed:SEED is planned, and a checker in the Wasm tests confirms that every trapping instruction is preceded by an explicit check (D554). It respects the measured toolchain: no Rust to wasm32 (D550), no statepoints, no JSPI or WasmFX. Its risk table (section 8) is concrete.
scores.flaws: (1) Tail calls break. D510/D545 let a direct call return the raw bits of its i32, i64, f64 or bool return type, while the uniform entry used for call.clo returns ref. Take a closure or polymorphic wrapper that tail-calls a function returning raw Int64, or an Int64 function that tail-calls a polymorphic g returning ref. The box or unbox must run after the call, so the call is no longer in tail position and musttail is impossible. That violates §5.7 for the hof and dict cases of tail_calls.t. native 2.3 explains exactly this failure. (2) Wasm resume has no workable layout. D501 keeps structured control in KIR because 'WasmGC requires structured control', and D529 generates Wasm from KIR, not from bytecode. But D556's 'resume entry branches by position number into the middle of the body' cannot be expressed in nested structured blocks, because br targets only enclosing labels. Resumable functions need the flattened acyclic block layout anyway (uniform 6.10). (3) Wasm has two unwinding mechanisms: exnref for N, T, discard and errors (D555), and state-machine bubbling for G (D556). Q5 cancelresume needs a G capture taken inside a catch block, with the pending exnref saved in the frame struct and re-thrown with throw_ref on resume. This is deferred to M91 with no design. (4) The Wasm stack plan is only node --stack-size=..., with no RLIMIT raise (D554). Under the default 8 MiB rlimit, anything above about 7.8 MB segfaults (E15), so depth is capped near 127k minimal frames, and V199 accepts this as a known difference. My measurement shows that raising RLIMIT_STACK, or using a Worker with stackSizeMb, reaches 1e7 frames. (5) Limits use different units: native counts value-stack words (128M words, an unverified guess that D537 itself doubts), Wasm uses a depth counter. Backends reach the limit at different programs. (6) Math libraries differ: glibc natively (D539), but on Wasm only P233. In practice that means JS Math, whose results V8 computes independently of glibc. (7) In D542, with --tier=jit and the top-level driver calling JIT directly, no interp_run activation exists to process UNWIND or YIELD. The driver must embed that loop, and this is not stated.

best_ideas: Use a logical depth limit that is identical in the interpreter, the JIT, Wasm and Diktor's --run-ir: count non-tail calls, clause activations and resumed frames (uniform 3.13, D512). The exit-0-or-3 outcome then does not depend on tier-up timing or frame sizes. Keep a native-sp or V8 backup check, and treat it firing as a bug signal (exit 70).

Run Node with enough stack. Raise RLIMIT_STACK in the spawned child (setrlimit in pre_exec) and pass --stack-size at about 90% of it (uniform D521). The fallback is a Worker with resourceLimits.stackSizeMb. I measured both: ulimit -s 2000000 with --stack-size=1500000, and a Worker with stackSizeMb=1024, each ran the spike's non-tail even_nt to 1e7 frames.

Make every function return the uniform word. Allow unboxed arguments only, and give each function a uniform entry that unboxes and then musttails the direct entry (native 2.3). This is the only representation rule that keeps §5.7 through closures and polymorphic callees.

Give all JIT functions and stubs one tailcc prototype (the measured tailcc i64(ptr ctx)). Generate the stubs at startup as LLVM modules: a tailcc interp_stub, and a ccc-to-tailcc enter stub for Rust. Every tail edge into Rust goes through a tailcc stub, because tailcc-to-ccc musttail is rejected (sl tohost).

Interp-to-JIT tail calls: hand a request back to the stub or trampoline only when the frame is the bottom frame of the current interp_run activation. Otherwise pop the frame and call native code normally, so the next interpreter entry becomes a bottom frame and alternation stays bounded (native 4.8).

Deopt on yield (incremental D542). JIT frames have the interpreter's layout on the shared value stack. A YIELD or UNWIND simply returns to the interpreter loop, and captured frames resume in the interpreter, then re-enter the JIT through the entry table at the next call. The JIT then needs no resume switch, fibers or eh_frame.

Wasm re-entry: lower the acyclic LIR to topologically ordered, flat nested blocks with a br_table at the function head. Restore locals from the frame struct, then branch forward (uniform 6.10). This works for any DAG and needs no relooper.

Mark the trap-free semantics of prims in LIR: explicit checks for div/rem by zero, MIN/-1, f64-to-int range and NaN, array bounds, ref.cast and null. Add a post-lowering checker that every trapping Wasm instruction is guarded (incremental D554), because traps and RangeError cannot be caught in Wasm.

Effect classification N/T/G, computed once by the writer and re-verified by the reader. T clauses are called in place with handler_top shifted outward, and N clauses are destination-tagged unwinds. Only G needs capture, and G is exactly where the spec gives no space guarantee (fx 6.0).

Pin down the cancel-clause rule in IRSpec as one sentence: an unwind arriving from the body side whose destination is not this activation runs this handler's cancel once (native 4.9). Handle cancel escapes through a barrier that saves and restores the pending state and can itself be captured by G (uniform 6.6.3).
Return a 0x2 sentinel in the return register in addition to (or instead of) the ctx state word, so the post-call check is cmp/je with no memory load (native D531).

Staging: get the full path working end to end first (Diktor KIR, then the RustKeleut interpreter, then the cram shim). Build Diktor's reference IR evaluator. The first JIT compiles only functions without handlers. Use --tier=mixed/alternating:SEED and a shim-driven cram oracle (incremental M79-M89, uniform 6.9).

Build the float show and libm runtime for Wasm with one implementation shared with native. Use clang 22 --target=wasm32 with wasm-ld on C sources, which native measured, or Rust once a wasm32 target is installed. Do not write a second JS BigInt implementation.
Prune yield checks and resume points on calls whose effect row is closed and contains no user-handleable effect (uniform D526). Keep --no-yield-prune for differential checking.
must_fix: Tail calls versus representation: function returns must always be the uniform word, or else every rep-mismatched tail edge needs a proof that it stays a tail call. incremental's raw-bits returns (D510/D545) break §5.7 for closure and polymorphic tail calls.

Specify the interp-to-JIT tail transition for a non-bottom interpreter frame (pop the frame, then a native call). Specify how the generic interp_stub learns the callee: a ctx->callee field, or env as in native. Specify the ccc-to-tailcc enter stub. uniform 6.9 and incremental D546 only describe the bottom-frame case.

Node stack policy: raise RLIMIT_STACK in the child and pass --stack-size, with a Worker using stackSizeMb as the fallback; both are now measured at 1e7 frames. Drop native's startup probe and 4000-level default, and drop incremental's flag-only plan, which is capped near 127k frames.

Make one stack-limit rule deterministic across interp, JIT, Wasm and Diktor --run-ir: a logical depth limit. Then measure the worst-case native and V8 bytes per logical level, covering Rust interp_run frames when tiers alternate non-tail and Liftoff frames of the largest functions. Size the reserved stack from that measurement rather than from an assumed 1 KiB.
Wasm G resume needs a flat CFG layout (DAG nested blocks plus br_table). It cannot re-enter structured KIR, so incremental D501/D529/D556 contradict each other.

Do not depend on JSPI or WasmFX for v1 G semantics. WasmFX needs a flag and crashes on switch. JSPI is asynchronous and has fixed 984 KB stacks that the global depth counter does not protect. If JSPI stays as an experiment, the per-stack limit must be accounted for.

Implement the subtle unwinding cases (Q5: cancelresume, cancelresumevia, cancelresumetwo, cancelsame, cancelperform) with one mechanism shared by all backends if possible. If two mechanisms remain (fibers versus bubbling, or exnref plus bubbling), each must pass these tests as a separate acceptance gate, along with tail_calls.t retry*.

Wasm runtime build: Rust wasm32-unknown-unknown is not installed (verified: the sysroot has only x86_64, rust-wasm is not installed). Either make installing it an explicit owner action in the first milestone, or use clang wasm32 C. Do not commit an opaque binary.
Use one libm and float-show algorithm for every RustKeleut backend, with the bitwise check run in CI. Record the difference from Diktor's glibc as a known difference (V/P entries).

Keep statepoints out. Define the rooting discipline: JIT spills every live word across every call that can allocate or switch, which in practice is every Keleut call. Rust runtime functions holding Keleut values across an allocation must use explicit Root handles. Safepoints occur only at allocation.

Price the JIT before committing to it: all-in-memory arguments and slots, per-entry resume checks, per-call state and depth checks, and v1 boxing of Int64/Float64 at function boundaries. Benchmark interp versus JIT early, in the JIT milestone, against a compiler-like workload.
Do not freeze IR 1.0 before both producer and consumer pass differential tests (native M79). Use 0.y with exact matching until then.

With --tier=jit, the top-level driver must contain the UNWIND and YIELD processing loop when no interp_run activation exists (incremental D542). Every Rust builtin that calls user code (Array.each, pinned) must either be written in KIR or propagate the sentinel or state, and root its values.

scores.design: uniform.md (KIR tree + shared LIR lowering, state-word propagation everywhere, yield bubbling, logical depth)
scores.strengths: Of the three, this one does the most to make results identical across backends, because every rule that decides meaning lives in one place. (1) One shared KIR->LIR lowering (2, 6.4) holds evaluation order, pattern guards, numeric checks, init checks, the effect protocol and depth. The LIR is defined as "never traps, no UB" (6.4 step 7, rustkeleut/doc/lir.md). That covers MIN/-1, MIN%-1, zero division and the f64->int range check with an open upper bound (fid 1). (2) Escape and capture use one mechanism, the state word (D508/D520, 6.6), in interp, JIT and Wasm alike. exnref, landingpad and fibers are banned in v1, so the cancel ordering of section 13.6 is implemented once. 6.6.6 traces cancelperform, cancelsame, cancelresume, resumeinner* and retry through that protocol. (3) The tail-call cases are covered explicitly. All JIT functions share one type, tailcc i64(ptr ctx) (D518), so every tail call can be musttail, which is the measured shape (tg 3.3). rt_handle tail-calls the return clause and the N-clause body (6.6.3 steps 2 and 4), G-clause tail resume replaces the caller with rt_resume (6.6.5), and T clauses return at the perform site, so tail resume runs in constant space. (4) The stack limit is a deterministic logical depth, default 1,000,000 (D512, 3.13). Diktor's --run-ir counts depth the same way, so overflow happens at the same point on every backend, runs cancel clauses and exits with 3. Tests pin the limit with --max-depth (8.3). (5) Float64 show, libm and string comparison are written once in keleut-rt-core and built for native and wasm32 (D515). JS formatting is rejected with measurements (6.5). (6) It catches that the moment of method selection is observable. opcall picks the method after the operands, call(method(...)) picks it first (3.5, interp.ml:340-345), which matters for inst.kel. (7) D535 states when init checks may be elided and gives a counterexample. Builtins such as Array.each and pinned are written in KIR (D533). The verifier recomputes tail marks and the N/T/G class (D506/D507). Conformance runs alternating=SEED tier combinations and --no-yield-prune (8.2), and ki/kj/ka/kw must match exactly with no known-diff exemptions (D499).
scores.flaws: (a) The Wasm runtime core depends on wasm32-unknown-unknown (D515, 6.10, M79), and native.md measured that this machine has neither a wasm32 rust-std nor rustup. M79 will fail as written, so the fallback in P239 (install it or commit an rt.wasm with its hash) has to become the plan. (b) For uniform depth on Wasm, D521 assumes V8 honours a large --stack-size once RLIMIT_STACK is raised. That is unverified (V198), and the stated fallback ("lower the Wasm limit and record a known diff") makes the same program end 0 on native and 3 on Wasm. (c) 6.6.2 says nothing about running depth_dec on the ERROR/DISCARD propagation path, and gives no headroom for cancel clauses. At the limit, the first call inside a cancel clause could fail again and be suppressed, which changes so.kel's 'startcancel ran'. (d) Logical depth is defined at KIR level (3.13: non-tail call, opcall, clause activation, builtin callback), but LIR step 10 puts depth_inc on every non-tail LIR call. That includes the rt_handle->body call and rt_resume frames, which KIR does not count, and M89 inlining could remove counted calls. Diktor --run-ir and RustKeleut can then disagree near the limit. (e) Rust-side native recursion (GC mark, interp<->JIT stub nesting) is protected only by a backstop SP check that warns (6.5). (f) The REPL is out of scope (D530), so RustKeleut does not provide sections 6.6 and 18.5. (g) Diktor (glibc) and RustKeleut (libm crate) give different sin/cos/exp/log bits, accepted as a known diff (D527). The plan needs a LangSpec section 17 statement (P237) to be consistent. (h) A Wasm trap goes to exit 70, not 3. The design relies on there being no missed checks, and there is no mechanical checker that every trapping instruction is guarded.

scores.design: native.md (Kerno ANF, fibers for G natively, 0x2 sentinel unwinding, exnref + JSPI/bubbling on Wasm)
scores.strengths: Native effects closely mirror OCaml 5's match_with/continue/discontinue (4.9), so cancel ordering on native, including cancelresume, follows Diktor's structure. 2.9 states the abstract machine and the single own-cancel rule as normative IRSpec text, which is good spec work. D502 keeps every function return uniform (w), with the reasoning that unboxed returns would destroy tail calls (2.3), which is correct. The UB-avoidance list is complete (D529), out-of-range literals become fail lit_range and must not be folded (D517), and the instance check sits at the method site (2.5). Emission is deterministic (2.6) and the f64 pattern uses IEEE == (D509). Strings are byte arrays, output is written in 64 KiB chunks through linear memory with fs.writeSync (D542), and REPL work is planned (M94). It is the only proposal that measured the toolchain gap: no wasm32 rust-std, but clang plus wasm-ld works.
scores.flaws: (a) There are three or more distinct escape/continuation mechanisms: native fibers plus the 0x2 sentinel (D531/D538), Wasm exnref (D541), and Wasm G via JSPI, with yield bubbling as a fallback chosen only at M90. The cancel ordering of section 13.6 has to be implemented and verified separately for each. JSPI is asynchronous and suspends only to the nearest promising boundary, which does not match synchronous clause/body round-trips or nested handlers where the perform goes to an outer handler (fx 4, incremental D556 alt 1), so Wasm G semantics are undecided. (b) The default limit is native stack (D530: 1 GiB main fiber, SP check at entry), and the deterministic --depth-limit is for tests only ('JIT does not count by default'). Interp and JIT frames differ in size and translation runs on another thread (D536), so for deep recursion whether the program ends 0 or 3 depends on timing and tier. (c) G handler bodies run on 64 MiB fibers, and the number of active fibers is capped at 100,000 (D539, V208). The same recursion can succeed outside a G handler and fail inside one, or fail on native but not on Wasm. (d) The Wasm depth limit is probed at startup: half the RangeError depth, or 4,000 if probing fails (D543). That makes results depend on the machine and even on the run. A 4,000 default is far below Diktor's 1M. (e) There are two Float64 show implementations, Rust {:.*e} and a JS BigInt version (D527), and two libms, the Rust libm crate and musl C built with clang (D528). They are equivalent only by sampling (V203, 1M cases), and clang's default fp-contract can change bits. (f) Operators are lowered to method calls in ANF (2.2), with no statement that the method is selected after the operands. The callee-first ANF rule would select the instance before the operands run, so inst.kel's ordering (before -> error) can diverge from Diktor. (g) It does not say that the return clause runs after the handler record is popped (section 13.6: no own cancel for errors in the return clause). (h) It says LangSpec need not change (P250), yet it defines observable behaviour (resume(resume) order, f64 pattern equality) only in IRSpec.

scores.design: incremental.md (KIR structured ANF, value-stack segments, JIT YIELD/UNWIND falls back to interpreter, exnref + state machine on Wasm)
scores.strengths: Native effects have a single implementation. JIT frames have the same shape as interpreter frames, and YIELD/UNWIND hand the frames to the interpreter loop (D542). Capturing a continuation therefore works like deoptimization, and interp/JIT/mixed share one cancel implementation (D540/D541), with in-progress unwinds kept as value-stack frames so cancelresume (Q5) falls out naturally. JIT scope grows in stages (D547). Diktor's kir_eval follows the spine path for resume(resume) (D518). Per-use memoization is allowed only for syntactically-Lambda initializers (D507), the most conservative rule of the three. Wasm trap guards come with a checker that verifies them (D554). The Wasm G state-machine scope is driven by effect rows (D503/D556). The Diktor-only via-ir oracle runs before any Rust exists (5.2). known-diffs.toml fails on any unregistered diff (D562), IR tables are dumped and compared (5.4), and the REPL is included (M98).
scores.flaws: (a) It breaks constant-space tail calls. D510 and D545 let direct calls and returns use the declared representation, so a function with an i32/i64/f64/bool return gives back raw bits, and only the uniform entry returns ref. A tail call from a function returning Int32 or Int64 to a polymorphic or higher-order function returning ref, such as `f(x): Int32 = id(x)` or `loop(n) = apply(loop, n-1)`, needs an unbox after the call. It is then no longer a musttail, which violates section 5.7 (tail calls to higher-order functions). native.md D502 identified exactly this hazard. (b) For extern "C", native calls the host glibc and Wasm is left unresolved, declared implementation-defined with a known Wasm diff (D539, P233). That is a deliberate result divergence inside RustKeleut, and it ties native output to the host libm version. LLVM must also not constant-fold or intrinsify these calls, which the plan does not state. (c) There are two Float64 show implementations, Rust (D534) and JS BigInt (D553). (d) Wasm uses exnref for N/T/errors (D555) but a heap state machine for G (D556). Q5, a G operation performed inside a cancel during unwinding, is deferred to M91 with no named mechanism. Bubbling out of a try_table catch block means parking the exnref in the frame and rethrowing on resume, and nobody has checked that this can be expressed. (e) The limits do not agree. Native counts total value-stack words, with a 128M default that the plan itself says is unconfirmed and may contradict fid 5 (D537). The OCAMLRUNPARAM l= mapping is a heuristic (D561). Wasm uses a depth counter bounded by a depth measured with minimal frames (D554), so large-frame functions can hit an uncatchable RangeError, with no cancel and no exit 3, before the counter fires. Deep recursion is accepted as a known diff (V199). (f) If the 4 GiB native stack reservation fails, it retries with 256 MiB (risk table). Together with async JIT (D546), the native SP check can fire nondeterministically before the value-stack limit. (g) Operator->method lowering in ANF (2.2 step 5) says nothing about selecting the method after the operands (the inst.kel ordering). (h) It does not say whether the return clause runs outside the handler.

best_ideas: (uniform D512/3.13) A deterministic logical-depth limit, defined in IR semantics and implemented the same way by interp, JIT, Wasm and Diktor --run-ir. Overflow becomes an ordinary runtime error that runs cancel clauses and exits 3 at the same point on every backend.

(uniform 6.4/D508) One shared lowering whose instructions are specified as trap-free and UB-free. Backends translate it mechanically. Evaluation order, numeric checks (div/rem MIN/-1, f64->int with an open upper bound), pattern guards, init checks and the effect protocol are decided once.

(uniform 6.6) One escape/capture protocol (a state word with YIELD/DISCARD/ERROR) on every backend, with a barrier for cancel clauses that can itself be captured mid-unwind (cancelresume) and state injection to discard continuations. Native fibers and exnref stay as later optimizations that must pass the full conformance matrix.

(incremental D542) JIT frames identical in layout to interpreter frames, so YIELD/UNWIND hand frames to the interpreter (deopt without a separate deopt mechanism). Continuations then cross tiers trivially.
(uniform D515) One runtime core for Float64 show (the {:.*e} search, 0 diffs against glibc in 2M cases), libm and string comparison, compiled for native and Wasm. Never use JS number formatting.
(uniform 3.5) Separate opcall (method selected after the operands) from call(method(...)) (selected first), so the observable timing of instance-declared-before-use errors matches Diktor (inst.kel).

(native D502) Make function returns always uniform so tail calls between functions with different return representations stay musttail. Unboxed-return entries only where every tail-call target agrees.
(native 2.9) State Q1-Q10 and the one-sentence own-cancel rule as normative text in an IRSpec abstract machine.
(uniform D506/D507, incremental 1.7) Verifier recomputes tail marks, the tail-resume spine and the N/T/G class from the structure and rejects any mismatch.
(uniform D535) Init-check elision rule with an explicit counterexample test (a closure created in an earlier def_value calling a later global).
(incremental D554) Mechanical checker that every Wasm instruction that can trap (div_s, rem_s, trunc, array.get, ref.cast, null deref) has an explicit guard in front of it.
(incremental D507) Allow per-use memoization only when the initializer is syntactically a Lambda; document Diktor's da_last under that condition.

(uniform 8.2 / native 6.1 / incremental D562) A conformance matrix including seeded alternating tiers, --gc-stress and --no-yield-prune. Interp, JIT, mixed and Wasm must agree exactly, and any diff not registered in known-diffs fails.
(incremental 5.2 / uniform DIKTOR_VIA_IR) A Diktor-only via-IR run of all cram, to validate the emitter and IR semantics before any Rust exists.
(uniform D533 / incremental D538) Write Array.each, pinned and the runtime wiring in KIR, so effects performed inside callbacks can be captured on every backend.
(native 2.6) Deterministic IR emission tested byte for byte across processes; stable names independent of OCaml oids.
must_fix: Function return representation must not break section 5.7. Either all returns are uniform (native D502, uniform 6.4 step 4), or the IR verifier rejects tail marks whose caller and callee return reps differ, and the writer boxes so that every tail call stays musttail. incremental D510/D545 currently violate this for Int32/Int64/Float64/Boolean-returning functions that tail-call polymorphic or higher-order functions.

Make the resource limit deterministic and the same on every backend. Define it at IR level, so LIR-internal calls (rt_handle body, rt_resume frames) and inlining cannot change the count. Decrement it on the unwind path and keep a reserve so cancel clauses can run at the limit. Use the same count in Diktor --run-ir. Never probe at startup (native D543) or depend on native SP or async JIT timing (native D530, incremental D537).

Before relying on it, verify that Node/V8 can be given more stack than the logical limit needs (RLIMIT_STACK plus --stack-size, or Worker stackSizeMb; uniform V198, native V202). Otherwise V8's RangeError escapes wasm catch, so no cancel clauses run and the exit is not 3.

Decide one escape/continuation mechanism, or prove equivalence. If Wasm keeps exnref while native uses state words or fibers, the six never_ops cancel tests plus preresume, err, clauseerr, clausestop, cancelerr, cancelnever and retry must pass on every backend and every seeded tier mix. JSPI must not be the G mechanism (it is asynchronous and suspends only to the nearest promising boundary). Q5 (a G operation inside cancel during unwinding) needs a named mechanism on Wasm.

Use one Float64 show implementation for all backends, or a bit-exact oracle run on every backend: fid's 2M cases, powers of two, exact-halfway cases, -0.0, NaN printed without sign, the 1e16 boundary.

Use one libm for every RustKeleut backend, statically included rather than the host glibc, and called through opaque runtime symbols so LLVM cannot fold or intrinsify it. If C is compiled for Wasm, pin the source and use -ffp-contract=off. Document the divergence from Diktor's glibc as implementation-defined in LangSpec section 17.

Settle the wasm32 toolchain question. This machine has no wasm32 rust-std and no rustup (measured in native.md). Either install the target, or vendor a hashed rt.wasm, or use clang. Make that the plan of record, not a contingency.

IRSpec must fix observable selection and evaluation order: an operator-derived method is selected after the operands (inst.kel), named constructor arguments in written order with storage in declaration order, record extend/update order, and resume's argument evaluated before the already-resumed check. Verify with order.kel, order2.kel and inst.kel on all tiers.
State explicitly that the return clause runs after the handler is popped (no own cancel on errors there), and likewise for N-clause bodies and the code after a resume returns.

Guarantee Wasm never traps, and check it mechanically. Guard div/rem (including MIN/-1 and MIN%-1), trunc, array bounds, ref.cast and null. A trap that slips through is an internal error, not exit 3, so it has to be designed out.

Make byte output exact end to end. fs.writeSync must loop on short writes and handle EAGAIN when stdout is a non-blocking pipe. Large strings are chunked. There is no JS-string conversion on any path. stdout is flushed before stderr diagnostics. The child node's exit status and stdout bytes pass through unchanged. A write failure unwinds with cancel and exits 74.
Native runtime code must not recurse unboundedly on the native stack (iterative GC marking, bounded nesting of interp<->JIT stubs), so deep data or deep stacks cannot SIGSEGV instead of exiting 3.

Out-of-range numeric literals are an evaluate-time error that constant folding must not hoist or remove. Uninitialized globals and instances keep a check wherever a closure created earlier can run before initialization.
Section 6.6 / 18.5 REPL semantics (rejected input rolled back, output not retracted) are eventually needed for full fidelity. The uniform design omits the REPL entirely.

Document in LangSpec the decisions the designs make implicitly: Float64 literal pattern equality uses IEEE == (section 11.1), the resume(resume) order (section 13.5), and libm results are implementation-defined (section 17). Pick one exit code for IR verification failure (65 or 70) and record it as implementation-defined.
